children: Round-up of South Korean financial markets:
** South Korean shares rose more than 1% on Friday, led by gains in chipmakers, but still posted a third consecutive weekly loss amid worries about high bond yields.
** The benchmark KOSPI
closed up 107.73 points, or 1.64%, at 6,687.21, marking its biggest daily rise since August 20. It ended the week down 1.5%.

** Wall Street rallied on Thursday as investors curbed their rate-hike bets after U.S. Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said he would support holding the Fed funds target rate steady if data shows inflationary pressures are abating.
** Chipmaker Samsung Electronics
rose 2.20% and peer SK Hynix
gained 3.20%, tracking overnight gains in U.S. peers.
** Among other index heavyweights, battery maker LG Energy Solution
slid 1.92%, while Hyundai Motor
was unchanged and sister automaker Kia Corp
was down 0.71%.
** Steelmaker POSCO Holdings
shed 1.46%, while drugmaker Samsung BioLogics
fell 2.03%.
** Of the total 909 traded issues, 549 shares advanced, while 309 declined.
** Foreigners were net buyers of shares worth 479.3 billion won ($354.89 million).
** Financial investment firms bought 1.2 trillion won, according to Korea Exchange data, while other corporations bought 1.6 trillion won, which analysts said likely reflected share buybacks.
** The won was quoted at 1,350.4 per dollar on the onshore settlement platform
, 0.43% higher than its previous close at 1,356.2.
** The currency hit its strongest level since early July 2025.
** In money and debt markets, September futures on three-year treasury bonds (KTBc1) gained 0.04 point to 103.18.
** The most liquid three-year Korean treasury bond yield (KR3YT=RR) fell by 0.4 basis points to 3.884%, while the benchmark 10-year yield
fell by 1.3 basis points to 4.350%.
